sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352. doi:10.26512/rbla.v6i2.16285.
sources.note: No statement on Uirina prosody. The only phonological content is general, on Natterer's notation (pp.339-340): 'he made ample use of diacritic signs, most of which are difficult to interpret today'; in Bororo the acute on é marks a central vowel, elsewhere a mid front vowel ('The motivation behind these different uses of é is not clear'); a hiatus in his handwriting marks a glottal stop. It also remarks that Cabixí 'may have been tonal judging from its structure and the diacritics'. Relevance for uiri1238: the accent marks in the Uirina list (Martius's collapá, idâ, camoê..) cannot be read as…

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. Bd. II: Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. 'UIRINA' list p.229 (p.252 of the Google/archive.org scan bub_gb_B3z7W40v4oAC).
sources.note: Nothing. One page (~85 Latin-glossed items) of Natterer's vocabulary with a footnote locating the 'Horde der Uirina oder Uarira' on the Rio Marari; forms carry unexplained diacritics (collapá, idâ, camoê, dadarró, bicurô, hê tî, dáamanâ). The volume's only remark on the acute (pp.28-30) is a general Tupi-orthography note ('den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen'), not a statement about Uirina.

sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1817-1835 [Uirina list c.1830-31]. Wortlisten von Indianersprachen in Brasilien. Manuscript, Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH T 2 (Nachlass J.J. von Tschudi), 2 boxes; digitized on e-manuscripta (online since 2022-03-02), doi:10.7891/e-manuscripta-128842. Images [621]-[624]: 'Nacaõ Uirina / Palavras da Giria delles' (fol. 41 / 192).
sources.note: Wordlist only (c.85 Portuguese-glossed items over 4 pages) with sporadic, unexplained diacritics (Mápa, Ápa, ámama, Atinâre, Ligé, Ládi, Litanaábe, Libatá, Camoê, uequenâ, Máaballe, Mauá, Pixé, cuibâ, Adá, Tabinâ, Metá, Ocollé, Camâ, Dá amanâ, Ammâ, Bacué, Idá, Mariá, hé tí, hájuaque, Liquê); no key to the marks and no remark on pronunciation anywhere on the four pages — accent MARKS in a wordlist, not a statement.
Nothing; en: 'known only from the wordlists of Johann Natterer and Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius'; pt reproduces Natterer's 1831 flora/fauna vocabulary after Ramirez 2020 vol.4.
